subject: Request: rate governance exemption & SLA alignment for Oct launch
messages:
From: Priscilla Tan <priscilla.tan@osirishealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: rate governance exemption & SLA alignment for Oct launch

Diego / Aditya,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. We're ramping toward a targeted pilot launch on the week of Oct 26 and have an anticipated 3x burst in inference traffic for a 48-hour window driven by patient onboarding flows. Our current concern is hitting Redwood's fairness throttles and experiencing degraded latency for critical front-end calls.

Quick facts:
- Expected peak sustained QPS: ~220 (peak per minute bursts up to ~420)
- Typical request size: 700-1100 tokens (chat completions + structured function calls)
- Window: Oct 27 08:00 PDT -> Oct 29 08:00 PDT (48 hrs)
- Non-negotiable latency target for UI keypaths: p99 <= 700ms

Can Redwood provide a short-term exemption to the default rate governance (burst ceilings/fairness scheduling) or a prioritized routing policy for this window? We are open to a limited temporary reserved pool or a canary priority policy (we can accept higher per-token costs).

I've attached our traffic extract (osiris_oct_traffic_pattern.csv) and a redline of the SOW with launch notes (osiris_sow_comments.docx). If you need a quick runbook of fallback behavior on our side, I can share it.

Appreciate if you can confirm what info/legal approvals you need and a rough timeline for a carveout decision.

Best,
Priscilla Tan
Head of Product, Integrations
Osiris Health
priscilla.tan@osirishealth.com
+1 415-555-0142


From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Priscilla Tan <priscilla.tan@osirishealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: rate governance exemption & SLA alignment for Oct launch

Priscilla — thanks for the detailed note and the attachments, very helpful. We can support you here; we just need to align on a short mutual action plan and a technical guardrail set to protect both parties.

High-level plan we typically use for short-term launch carveouts:
1) Traffic validation: Redwood will run a pre-launch replay against a canary pool to validate p99 latency at requested QPS.
2) Temporary reservation: create a time-boxed reserved capacity slice for Oct 27 08:00 -> Oct 29 08:00 with explicit burst headroom and higher cost profile.
3) Fairness override rules: during the window, your traffic will be routed to a priority queue; fairness score decay will be adjusted to avoid your requests being deprioritized for short bursts.
4) Fallback policy: we will provide a model fallback chain (lower cost/latency variants) with automated traffic shifting if p99 targets are missed.

Info we need from you by EOD Wed:
- Confirm the exact UTC timestamps for the 48-hr window (we currently have PDT times).
- A signed temporary amendment that limits the carveout to the specified window and includes a high-water pricing uplift (we'll share a template).
- Any regulatory constraints (PII redaction, regional routing) — note that Private deployments have different controls.

I've looped Marissa (account lead) and Lauren (CS) to draft the amendment and validate the SLOs. We'll also run the replay on our staging fleet starting Oct 24.

Attachments: none in this reply.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priscilla Tan <priscilla.tan@osirishealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: rate governance exemption & SLA alignment for Oct launch

Priscilla — appreciate the traffic file. I've sketched a temporary amendment and a technical approach that balances your p99 requirement and our platform fairness obligations. Key points in the proposal (attached as redwood_temp_amendment_v1.pdf):

- Reserved slice: 4 x A100-equivalent vCPU pool (timeboxed) to cover sustained 220 QPS with headroom to 450 QPS for minute-level spikes.
- Pricing uplift: +45% over standard hosted rate for the reserved slice and burst consumption.
- Fairness adjustment: fairness score decay set to 1.2x for the 48-hr window (minimizes deprioritization).
- Automated fallback chain: primary model (redwood-gpt-13b-std) -> fallback latency-optimized model (redwood-lite-6b) -> async batch queue for retries.
- Success criteria: p99 <= 700ms for the primary model over a 30-minute rolling window for >90% of samples during the window. If the criteria fail for two consecutive 30-minute windows we will trigger automated rollback to fallback chain and notify your on-call.

Operational notes:
- We will run a replay job on Oct 24 to validate end-to-end latency. Diego, please confirm the replay dataset and the staging tag we should use.
- Legal will require a signed temporary amendment; Finance will confirm uplift invoicing. We can do DocuSign routing to the contacts in Priscilla's email.

Attachments: redwood_temp_amendment_v1.pdf

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Priscilla — all set from our side. Quick summary of next steps and owners:

- Oct 22 EOD: Osiris to confirm exact UTC timestamps and sign-off on the amendment (Priscilla)
- Oct 24: Redwood replay on staging (Diego/Infra team) — we will run the replay tag: replay/osiris/oct24/v1
- Oct 25: Finance/Legal to route DocuSign for the temporary amendment (Marissa) — link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-temp-amendment
- Oct 27 08:00 PDT: Reserved slice activation (Redwood Ops)

Priscilla, once you sign the amendment we'll provision the reserved slice and schedule a 30-minute prep call on Oct 26 to walk through escalation steps and confirm on-call contacts. Attaching the amendment we discussed for quick review.

Attachments: redwood_temp_amendment_v1.pdf
